translations.text: Wash yourselves and be clean. Remove the evil of your souls from before my eyes; abandon your wickedness.
Therefore the Lord of hosts says this: Woe to the mighty men of Israel! My wrath against my adversaries will not cool, and I will take vengeance on my enemies.
For the eyes of the Lord are exalted, but humanity is lowly.
At that time people will cast out the unclean idols of gold and silver that they made to worship what is worthless.
At that time he will answer him and say: I will not be your ruler, for I have neither food nor clothing in my house. I will not be a ruler of this people.
And they said: Let us bind the righteous man, for he is troublesome and burdensome to us.
Why do you oppress my people and shame the face of the poor?
Those who remain in Zion and those left in Jerusalem will be called holy—all who are recorded to live in Jerusalem.
It will be a shade from the heat and a covering under which to shelter from dew and rain.
What more, then, shall I do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? Look, I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will tear down its fence, and they will plunder it. I will remove its wall, and it will become a place to be trampled.
They drink wine while singing to the lyre, drum, and flute. They drink wine but do not consider the work of the Lord or look at the deeds of his hands.
People will be brought low, humanity will be humbled, and the eyes of the proud will be lowered.
They will graze like oxen that have been taken captive. They will graze like sheep in a field, seeking food in their pasture.
They will neither hunger nor thirst; they will neither grow weary nor sleep. They will not loosen their belts from their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
For before the child knows good and evil, he will reject evil and choose what is good.
And the Lord said to me: Take a large, new sheet of papyrus and write on it with a human pen these words: Quickly summon and plunder.
Honor the Lord as holy, and he will be the one you fear.
And if you trust in him, he will sanctify you and will not make you stumble like a stumbling stone or like a rock that makes you slip.
The bricks have fallen. Come, let us quarry stone; let us cut down sycamores and cedar as a foundation for ourselves.
Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, nor will he have mercy on their orphans and widows, for they are all wicked and hostile, and every mouth speaks injustice.
And even if they say to him: Are you alone a ruler?
Those who remain of Jacob will find strength in the Lord.
Therefore the Lord of hosts says this: My people who live in Zion, do not fear Persia, for he will strike you with a rod. For I will bring my scourge upon you, so that you may see the road to Egypt.
And the Lord will bring a scourge upon them like the scourge of Midian in the land of affliction; and his spear will be directed toward the sea route and along the road toward Egypt.
And the spirit of the fear of the Lord will fill him.
But he will judge with gentle judgment and rebuke the nobles of the earth. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and the sinner with the breath of his lips.
And the Lord will dry up the sea of Egypt and stretch out his hand over the river with a powerful wind. He will strike seven ravines so that people may cross them wearing sandals.
And on that day you will say, “I praise you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned away your punishment and again had mercy on me.”
Raise a banner on the mountains of the wilderness. Raise your voices and strengthen your hands. Let the rulers open the gates.
And because of this, every hand will grow weak and every soul will be terrified.
And the leaders will be thrown into confusion, and pain will seize them like a woman giving birth. They will fight among themselves; they will be tormented, and their faces will blaze like fire.
Then the stars of heaven, those of Orion, and the whole heavenly realm will not shine. The sun will grow dark at its rising, and the moon will not shine.
And those who remain will be more precious than gold and silver, and a person will be more precious than a sapphire gem.

And all this will happen quickly and will not be delayed. The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. They will rest in their own land, and foreigners will join them and be added to the house of Jacob.
For the Lord has shattered the yoke of sinners and the yoke of rulers.
And the trees of Lebanon and the cedars of Lebanon will rejoice over you: “Since you were laid down, no one has come up to cut us down.”
And you too will be cast into the mountains like an unclean corpse, with the many corpses of those pierced by the spear, who go down into Sheol.
And what will the kings of the nations say? “Look, the Lord has founded Zion, and because of this the humble among the people will be saved.”
Mourn for yourselves, because Dibon has been destroyed, where your idol dwells and where your sacrifices are.
And the waters of Nimrim will dry up, and its grass will perish; no greenery will be found within it.
I will send them like wild animals into a rocky land.
This is the word that the Lord spoke concerning Moab, which he spoke long ago.

And when you plant, you will go wrong, and what you sowed will bear fruit in the morning, at harvest, on the day you pass on your inheritance. And like a father to his son, you too will pass on an inheritance to your children.
Toward evening they will lament; before morning comes, it will be no more for them.
Woe to the land of ships that have wings, among the rivers of Ethiopia!
And the fishermen will mourn, and all who lower their fishing gear into the river will weep. Those who spread their nets and the fishermen will lament.
And those who work at it will suffer, and all who work with the equipment will [?], and their souls will suffer.

And it will be a sign for the Lord in the land of Egypt forever. For they will cry out to the Lord because of those who oppress them, and he will send them a man who will save them. He will judge him and save him.
Like a storm from the wilderness, it passed through the desert and came from a fearsome land.
For this is what the Lord said to me: Within a year, reckoned as a hired worker's year, the glory of the descendants of Kedar will come to an end.
They also tore down the houses of Jerusalem and the fortification that protected the city.
Look, the Lord of hosts will strip you of your clothing and the crown of your glory.
At that time I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah.

I will dress him in your clothing and give him your crown. I will entrust him with your administration and give him your authority. I will transfer everything in your hands into his hands. He will be a father to those who live in Jerusalem and those who live in Judah.
Their multitude will melt away, and their defenses will fall, for the Lord, who has power, will reign in Zion and Jerusalem and will be glorified before the elders.
For the sinner who does not learn righteousness on earth and does not do good has come to an end.
Add misfortune to them, Lord; add misfortune to the honored people of the earth.
As a woman in labor, nearing childbirth, cries out in her pain, so it was with your beloved.
Because of our fear of you, Lord, we conceived, suffered labor pains, and gave birth to the spirit of your salvation on earth.
Who will appoint me to guard stubble in the wilderness? Because of this I fought against her [?].
Those who are coming are the descendants of Jacob, for Jacob and Israel will sprout and bear fruit, and his fruit will fill the world.
At that time the Lord will close off the area from the river's channel to Rhinocorura.
The flower that falls from the confidence of their glory on the summit of the high mountain will be like an early fig: whoever sees it runs to it and wants to swallow it before taking it in his hand.

For these people became drunk on wine, and mead led them astray. Mead bewildered the priest and the prophet, and wine overwhelmed them. They went astray in drunkenness, and this is a deception of the eyes.
With sinful lips and in another language they will speak to this people.
Your oath with death will be annulled, and your covenant with Sheol will not stand.
As soon as it comes, it will sweep you away. Every morning your day will draw near to you, and at night there will be an expectation of evil.
The Lord will rise like a rock of sinners and will be in the valley of Gibeon. He will do his work in wrath—a bitter work. He will make his wrath astonishing, and his fury extraordinary.
Does he not, after leveling his field, sow a little black cumin and cumin, and then sow wheat and barley?
The wealth of sinners will be like dust from [?] and like chaff carried by the wind. At that time it will come suddenly from the Lord of hosts.
They will give the book to a man who cannot read and tell him, “Read this.”
Will it not be only a little while before Lebanon becomes like Mount Carmel and Carmel becomes like a forest?
But the righteous offer wise counsel, and that counsel will endure.
Her houses. They will abandon the wealth of their cities and the inheritance of their houses. Their cities will remain in misery forever, a delight for wild donkeys and a pasture for animals.
Holy is the Lord who dwells on high, and Zion is filled with righteousness and justice.
The nations will be like burning thorns in the wilderness, burned and cast away.
Those in Zion have rebelled against me and wronged me. Look, trembling will seize the sinners.
Gather, people, and listen, angels. Let the earth and those in it listen, and the world and all the nations in it.
The Lord’s sword is filled with blood and laden with the fat of sheep, goats, and rams. For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in Edom.
Hedgehogs will breed there, and the earth will keep its young safe. Deer will meet there and see one another face to face.
He will give them their allotted share; his hand has given it to them as an inheritance, and they will graze there. They will inherit it forever, generation after generation, and rest in it.
At that time the eyes of the blind will regain sight, and the deaf will hear.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, Shebna, the army scribe, and Jehoiakim son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him what the Rabshakeh had said.
King Hezekiah’s servants arrived before Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: ‘This is what the Lord says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the king of Persia has insulted me.’”
Tell King Hezekiah of Judah this: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, ‘Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Persia.’”
Where are the kings of Hamath and Arpad, and of the cities of Sepharvaim, Menahe, and Gawan?
At that time Hezekiah became ill and was near death.
Isaiah said to him, “Listen now to the word of the Lord of armies.”
Look, the days are coming when everything in your house and everything your ancestors have stored up to this day will be taken and carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left for you.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all living beings will see the Lord’s salvation, for the Lord has spoken.
The grass withers and the flower falls, but the word of the Lord remains forever.
To whom will you compare the Lord? Whose likeness will you say is his equal?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Have you not been told from the beginning? Do you not know the foundations of the earth?
Who raised up the righteous one from the east and called him to follow in his footsteps? He brings terror before nations and kings.
Do not be afraid; I am with you. Be on your guard; do not let them deceive you. I am your God, who has strengthened you, helped you, and held you with my righteous right hand.
Tell us what is coming and what will happen afterward, so that we may know that you are gods. Do good and do harm, so that we may marvel at you, investigate, and know.
I have been silent since the creation of the world. Will I now remain silent forever? Will I endure like a woman giving birth [?]? I will wipe out and swallow up at the same time.
You keep seeing, but do not pay attention. Your ears are open, but you do not hear.
And now, this is what the Lord God says, who made you, Jacob, and who created you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have saved you and called you by name.
And I will say to the north: Bring them.
And to all those who are called by my name: For I created them and made them for my glory.
Be my witnesses, and I too will be a witness for you, says the Lord God, together with my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know, believe, and understand that I am he.
It is not now that I have called you, Jacob, nor have I wearied you, Israel.
I am the one who wipes out your sins and will not remember them.
This is what the Lord God who created you says: I will help you even in the womb. Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant, and Israel, my beloved, whom I have chosen.
For I will give water in thirst to those who travel through the wilderness, and I will place my spirit upon your offspring and my blessing upon your children.
For the craftsman sharpened the iron of his axe and made them. He hammered them with his hammer and strengthened them with the power of his arm. He also grows hungry and weak, and he becomes thirsty.
And from what remains he makes himself gods that he carves. He kneels and bows down to it, prays to it, and says to it: Save me, for you are my God.
I will go ahead of you and lower the mountains. I will break the bronze gates and shatter the iron bars.
Let heaven above rejoice, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness. Let the earth bring forth growth, and let it bring forth mercy and uprightness together. I am the Lord God who created you.

I have made you better and fashioned you like clay for a potter. Does the one who plows the ground plow all the time? Does clay say to the potter: What are you making? You cannot make anything, and you have no hands. Does clay argue with the one who molds it?

This is what the Lord of hosts says: The labor of Egypt and the cities of Ethiopia, and the people of Seba, tall men, will come to you. They will become your servants and follow behind you with their hands bound. They will bow down to you and pray to you, for God is with you, and there is no other God besides you.
For the Lord will save Israel with everlasting salvation. They will never be ashamed or disgraced.

And if they speak, let them draw near so that together they may know who made this known long ago. [?] when they told you that I am the Lord, and there is no other besides me, righteous and life-giving, and there is none like me.
To whom, then, will you compare me? Look and be wise, all of you who go astray.
Remember this and weep. Repent, you who have gone astray. Turn back and turn your hearts.
And remember the things of old and the things from the creation of the world, for I am God, and there is no other besides me.
I announce the former things and what will happen afterward before it happens, and then it happens.
I call a bird from the east and from a distant land for what I have planned. I have spoken and brought it about. I have created and done it. I brought him and prepared his way.
The one who saved you—his name is the Lord of hosts, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in shock and enter the darkness, daughter of Persia. You will no longer be called the power of a kingdom.
Stand now with your sorcery and your many spells, which you learned from your youth and which do not benefit you, to see whether any can save you.
And do not say: It is happening now and not long ago, and it is not what you heard in earlier days.
And if they thirst for water in the wilderness, he will bring water out of a rock for them. The rock will gush for them, water will flow, and my people will drink.
I will level the mountains for them, and every road will become pasture for them.
Can a woman [?] her child and have no mercy on the one she bore from her womb? Even if this woman forgets, I will not forget you.
Your children whom you lost will say in your hearing, “The land is too cramped for us. Make room for us where we can live.”
I will cover the sky with darkness and clothe it in sackcloth.
The Lord God became my helper. Therefore I was not ashamed. I made my face like solid rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah, who suffered labor pains for you. For he was only one when I called him, blessed him, loved him, and made him numerous.
Listen to me, listen to me, my people, and listen to my instruction, kings. For a law will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations.
I am the one who comforts you. Consider, then, whom you yourself have feared: a mortal man, a human being who withers like grass.
You have no one to comfort you among all the children you bore, and no one to stretch out his hand to you among all the children you raised.
Shake off your dust and rise. Jerusalem, sit down. Cast the chain from your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For this is what the Lord says: “I sold you for nothing, and it is not with gold that I will redeem you.”
As the Lord said: “My people first went down to Egypt and lived there as foreigners. Afterward they took them to the land of Persia in servitude.”
“And now, what has kept you here?” This is what the Lord says: “For they took my people for nothing. You were astonished and cried out.”
Let the deserted places of Jerusalem burst into rejoicing together, for the Lord has had mercy on her and has saved Jerusalem.
For you will not go out in turmoil, and you will not depart in flight.
“The Lord did not call you as an abandoned and fainthearted woman, nor as a woman hated from her youth,” says your God.
For look, I have made him trustworthy, a witness to the nations, a ruler and governor of the nations.
Let the sinner abandon his way and the unjust man his plans. Let him return to the Lord, and then he will have mercy on him, for he will abundantly forgive you your sins.
For you will go out with joy and be taught with gladness.
I will give them, in my house and in my resting place, a place that brings them renown, better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not perish.

And to those from another people who have come to the Lord, subjected themselves to him, and loved the Lord’s name; to those who have become his male and female servants; and to all who keep my Sabbaths without profaning them and hold firmly to my ordinance.
His burial will be in peace, for they will take him away from their midst.
You who delight in idols and offer sacrifices beneath leafy trees, and slaughter your children in the valleys among the clefts of the rocks.
On a great, high mountain you spread your bed; bring up your sacrifice there.
I will not punish you forever, nor will I always be angry with you, for the spirit comes from me, and I created every spirit.
But sinners will be tossed about like this and will find no rest.
“There is no joy for sinners,” says the Lord.

This is not the fast I have chosen, nor is it a day like this, when a person afflicts himself. Even if he bends his neck like a ring and lies down in sackcloth and dust, this is not a fast acceptable to the Lord.
They hatch serpents’ eggs and weave a spider’s thread. Whoever eats a serpent’s egg dies quickly, and if you break it open, a snake comes out.
They grope along walls like a blind person who has no eyes. They fall in broad daylight as though it were midnight, and they groan like people who are dying.
We have sinned and lied to you, and we have stopped following our God. We have spoken injustice and denied you; we have conceived and planned sinful things in our hearts.
Lift up your eyes, look around you, and see how your children have gathered. All your sons have come from far away, and your daughters are carried on shoulders.
The nations will build your walls, and their kings will stand before you. For in my anger I punished you, but in my mercy I brought you near.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor disgrace or destruction within your territory. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates will be engraved.
The sun will no longer give you light by day, nor will the moon shine for you by night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Like the produce of a flourishing field and like the seed of a garden, so the Lord will cause righteousness and joy to spring up before all the nations.
But whoever gathers it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gather it will drink it in my holy cities.
Why, Lord, have you led us astray from your way and hardened our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants and the people of your inheritance.
As wax melts before fire, so fire will consume your enemies, and your name will be made known among them.
Since the creation of the world, we have neither seen nor heard of another God besides you. You show your mercy to those who hope for your grace.
We have all become unclean, and all our righteousness is like a menstrual cloth. We have fallen like leaves because of our sins.
They sleep in the caves of dreamers, eat swine’s flesh, and defile the blood of their sacrifices and all their vessels.
Look, it is written before me. It will not remain silent until I repay, take vengeance, and return their recompense into their laps.

I will hand you over to war, and you will all die by slaughter. For I called you, and you did not answer me; I spoke to you, and you turned a deaf ear to me. You did evil before me, and you did not want me to save you.
She gives birth without suffering labor pains, she who is in labor, and she bore a male child.
“Just as the new heaven and the new earth that I make will remain before me,” says the Lord, “so your descendants and your name will endure.”
